uncertainty.interpretation: Judgment sensitivity, not a statistical interval; conditional quality comparisons only. If CAP falls to 3 because newly verified persistent destruction is established, the separate GQS ceiling of 5 would apply; these raw ranges do not assume that finding.

DUR.counterevidence: Signed space is not occupied revenue. Flexible coworking exits and an incomplete client backlog schedule limit confidence.

CAP.rationale: Low recent aggregate committed-capital productivity, without claiming private cohort IRRs or persistent mature destruction.
supporting_facts: FY23–FY26 incremental NOPAT of ₹1.69425 crore divided by incremental IC of ₹52.8078 crore is 3.2083%.
Earlier FY22–FY24 incremental returns were 20.196%; the FY26 conservative normalized increment is near zero.
CAP.counterevidence: Large immature CWIP and deposits depress current returns; better utilization could improve economics.

CASH.rationale: Mixed owner cash realization, largely explained by lease-deposit investment rather than impaired collections.
supporting_facts: Comparable FY24–FY26 CFO/PAT is 7.8857%, with ₹15.4369 crore invested in landlord deposits.
Before landlord investment and net of customer-deposit support, cash is ₹10.8105 crore. Receivables over one year fall from ₹0.5716 crore to ₹0.2960 crore.
CASH.counterevidence: Customer deposits rose ₹3.8891 crore and payables ₹2.9707 crore in FY26, supporting CFO. Deposits remain real capital needs.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Nukleus Office Solutions leases, fits out and operates flexible workspaces and enterprise managed offices. Organic revenue expanded rapidly, with managed offices now the main growth engine, but earnings per share and returns on the enlarged capital base do not yet establish a compounder. The decisive strength is demonstrated customer demand and an operating portfolio, not a unique technology moat. The decisive risks are upfront fit-out and landlord deposits, rent commitments before occupancy, related-party capital exposure and material new expense capitalization. At the last independently corroborated secondary trade of ₹173 on 14 October 2026, the shares are not demonstrably cheap after normalization. Classification: research hold for a new investment, with growth/execution rather than income or asset-liquidation economics. A complete monetary lease pipeline, funded rollout and renewal bridge, consistent cohort cash returns and executable market evidence could change this conclusion. This is not a finding of default, fraud or debt restructuring.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Exact issuer: Nukleus Office Solutions Limited, CIN L70101DL2019PLC355618, ISIN INE0VYX01018, BSE SME scrip 544370. Incorporated 27 September 2019; listed 4 March 2025. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026, research retrieval 22 October 2026. Normal market reference would be 19 October, but no authenticated issuer close for that date was recovered. ₹173 is a dated secondary last trade on 14 October, corroborated by two independent historical tables, not a current executable quote. On 4,032,000 issued shares it implies ₹69.7536 crore equity value. The official 19 October interoperability master confirms a 600-share lot; it does not establish NSE listing or make its price band a stock price. The illustrative ₹500,000 position is four lots/2,400 shares/₹415,200 below budget or five lots/3,000 shares/₹519,000 above it. Neither amount is guaranteed executable. Scope is standalone Indian GAAP/Accounting Standards, not consolidated Ind AS. The valuation horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, 1,826 days divided by 365.25, with nominal pretax INR equity hurdles of 12%, 15% and 18%. Confidence is High for observed audited totals and exact identity, Medium for reconciled earnings/capital economics and organic growth, Low for current lease obligations, unrestricted cash reconciliation and execution liquidity. Four gate conclusions and release conditions appear below.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: BQS is 4.86, displayed 4.9; GQS is 5.95, displayed 6.0. IAS remains NS: R, P and L cannot be responsibly scored from unsupported current funding and executable-price/liquidity evidence. The known IAS contribution is 1.815, original-weight coverage 45%, and mathematical missing-data bound 2.365–7.315, not a confidence interval or investment ranking. Each primitive appears once in each formula; the unrounded BQS feeds IAS. REV begins at 9 from 48.29% comparable three-year revenue CAGR, with zero trajectory adjustment and the Medium-confidence/history ceiling of 8. No governance or funding numerical override is triggered because there is no evidenced G1 or G3 failure. The GQS ceiling for CAP≤3 or CASH≤3 due to persistent destruction/poor cash realization is explicitly evaluated and not triggered: CAP4 reflects weak aggregate returns with an immature asset ramp, while CASH5 reflects explainable landlord-deposit investment, not persistently impaired receivable collection. This does not make the cash commitment harmless. GOV and CAP are the most uncertain primitives; moving both by one point changes BQS by 0.32 and CAP alone changes GQS by 0.15. Treat such differences as ties rather than spurious precision.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Customers pay monthly fees for ready-to-use shared offices or enterprise-specific managed workspaces, plus related services. Nukleus bears space sourcing, fit-out, operating service and collection obligations; customer security deposits are refundable funding, not revenue or permanent equity. Landlord deposits tie up cash separately. Management describes managed contracts of roughly four to nine years with matching property arrangements, while coworking clients may leave on one month's notice after lock-in. Actual matching obligations and client termination remedies were not fully disclosed. The FY26 presentation reports 25 centres, 4,373 seats, approximately 85% occupancy and 287 clients. Seventeen centres are coworking and eight managed offices. These are management portfolio metrics, not audited time-weighted cohorts. The final prospectus had 2,796 seats and 2,474 occupied at 31 December 2024, with wide centre-level occupancy dispersion, including new unoccupied offices. Counts of separate floors/managed offices are not independent buildings. Managed-office revenue rose from ₹9.6160 crore to ₹22.1666 crore, while coworking fell from ₹19.0891 crore to ₹13.3120 crore; managed share reached about 62.48%. Operational area is 3.06 lakh square feet in the deck, versus a less precise 3.6 lakh remark in the call; 7.39 lakh square feet under management is not all operational. Bangalore's completed but unavailable fit-out is a direct warning against equating footprint with revenue-producing space.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The useful advantages are existing locations, fit-out execution, local landlord relationships and enterprise service delivery. Longer client commitments can raise switching friction, but the company has not demonstrated network effects, defensible pricing power or a proprietary technology advantage. Management itself described a competitive/commodity market; proposed AI and integration initiatives do not establish realized unit-cost superiority. Larger peers provide relevant operating benchmarks, not automatic valuation comparables. Awfis's official FY26 deck reports ₹1,493 crore revenue, 266 centres, 184,000 seats, 76% blended and 84% mature occupancy. Smartworks reports ₹1,796 crore revenue and approximately 82% blended/89% mature occupancy, with normalized after-rent EBITDA of ₹314 crore. Both are far larger than Nukleus and have different portfolio maturity and contract structures. Awfis's headline Ind AS EBITDA cannot be compared directly to Nukleus's after-rent Accounting Standards earnings. EFC is a qualitative managed-workspace competitor; no unverified peer price multiple is imported. Location scarcity and client integration offer some friction, but additional competitors, client consolidation and a mismatch between lease lock-ins and customer exits can erode margins. MOAT3 therefore reflects limited demonstrated differentiation, not an assertion that the services lack value.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Audited revenue for FY22–FY26 is ₹3.4078, ₹10.8807, ₹17.1276, ₹28.7052 and ₹35.4785 crore. The comparable FY23–FY26 CAGR is 48.2869%; the four-year FY22–FY26 CAGR is 79.6275%. Five audited annual observations do not provide the six required for a five-year CAGR, so five- and ten-year rates remain ND. Annual absolute additions and growth percentages are embedded in the financial analysis. No subsidiaries, business combinations or acquired corporate revenue were identified; descriptions of acquiring office spaces refer to leasing/property access, not an acquired business. Growth is therefore organically generated at the issuer perimeter, but the split among opening seats, same-centre occupancy, price increases and services is not fully disclosed. Current trajectory is mixed rather than simply decelerating: H1FY26 revenue ₹16.9149 crore compares with derived H1FY25 ₹14.3304 crore; H2FY26 ₹18.5636 crore compares with ₹14.3748 crore. The two half-years support acceleration within FY26, while the full-year growth of 23.60% is below FY25. H2 PAT fell to ₹0.9720 crore from ₹1.1438 crore despite higher sales. No seasonal half-year is annualized into a current TTM forecast; the latest complete reported period remains FY26.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Enterprise demand, the existing NCR portfolio and signed space additions provide a plausible accessible runway, but a generic office-market TAM is not contracted revenue. The prospectus estimates roughly ₹2,200 per carpet square foot and 50 square feet per seat, implying ₹1.10 lakh fit-out per seat before landlord deposits and ramp losses. Three-to-six-month deposits, construction time and occupancy ramp can make an apparently profitable location initially cash-negative. April and May 2026 filings cover Shivaji Rcube Phase2, 12,000 square feet at Best Sky Tower and 75,000 square feet at Okaya; the July Gurugram lease adds another site. Financial rent, deposits, guarantees, full lock-ins and remaining committed capex are not comprehensively disclosed. These specific post-year-end obligations, not a generic demand for private daily bank statements, prevent a verified current funding bridge. Counterevidence is meaningful: ₹13.1329 crore face-value unused term/DOD/SOD capacity was disclosed at March end, but draw eligibility, collateral and January 2027 renewal matter. Aggregate FY23–FY26 incremental NOPAT/invested capital is only about 3.21%; the conservative normalization is near zero. Earlier FY22–FY24 increments were approximately 20.20%, so low recent returns cannot be called proven permanent mature-cohort destruction. Growth is real, but the presently enlarged capital base has not earned an established return above an illustrative 12% capital-cost benchmark. No company WACC estimate is implied.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The company reports delivery of a larger operating portfolio and a shift toward enterprise managed offices, but the Bangalore centre's ₹5.5033 crore fit-out remains unavailable because of landlord issues. The May 2026 ambition to exceed one million operational square feet by March 2027 is a dated target, not achieved capacity at the cutoff; the claimed 90% managed mix over three to four years is also prospective. Direct promoter holdings in the annual report total 69.61%; do not substitute an unverified 69.91% total-group claim or call the balance unrestricted free float. Related landlords hold ₹7 crore deposits, and Krishna Infosolutions has a ₹3.5 crore fit-out advance: together ₹10.5 crore, about 25.36% of equity. These disclosed commercial exposures create counterparty and minority-protection risk, but do not alone prove diversion. The prior ₹19.0115 crore related-party guarantee was removed in July 2025; escrow instalments paid through August 2025 were described as recovered. The FY26 secretarial report states the prior ROE-disclosure compounding matter was resolved; the penalty order/amount was not independently obtained. The full FY26 financial audit is unmodified, but explicitly emphasizes Bangalore, KMP/travel capitalization and deferred branding. ESOP Scheme-I 2026 for 201,600 options was approved at the September AGM. It is an authorized pool, not proven grants or exercise proceeds. The October facilities-manager resignation is not an auditor resignation. A separate feed label suggesting debt restructuring points to identical resignation bytes and is rejected as unsupported.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY26 reported PAT grew only 3.55% to ₹2.1353 crore while reported diluted EPS fell to ₹5.30 from ₹7.53 as the IPO share denominator became fully effective. Reported EBITDA ₹9.1734 crore contains ₹0.7156 crore other income; operating EBITDA excluding it is ₹8.4578 crore and operating EBIT ₹3.1461 crore. Newly capitalized KMP/travel ₹1.0933 crore and deferred brand spending ₹1.15 crore together produce conservative after-rent EBITDA ₹6.2145 crore and EBIT ₹0.9028 crore when fully expensed. EBIT is a lower-bound analytical adjustment, not a re-audit, because all recorded depreciation remains; a separate 0–₹0.10933 crore assumed KMP depreciation-overlap sensitivity is shown. Current-tax expense ₹1.3532 crore is offset by ₹0.6318 crore deferred-tax credit. The cash-flow tax-paid line equals both current expense and closing tax provision, while TDS receivable increases to ₹3.4940 crore; the reported CFO is preserved, but this is not independent proof of tax settlement. Full main audit, CARO and IFC were read: no reported borrowing default, bank-return disagreement, fraud or material going-concern uncertainty; audit-trail reporting is affirmative for FY26. These are counterevidence, not a guarantee of safety. FY24 prospectus CFO ₹10.9956 crore improperly includes financing borrowings for analytical operating-cash purposes. Removing ₹6.3885 crore borrowings and consistently reclassifying landlord/customer deposits reconciles to ₹4.2388 crore in the subsequent annual comparison. FY25 CFO −₹7.4589 crore is recast to −₹7.4403 crore in FY26, with an offsetting ₹0.0186 crore CFI difference. Comparable FY24–FY26 CFO totals ₹0.4254 crore against PAT ₹5.3946 crore, only 7.89%; however ₹15.4369 crore landlord-deposit investment explains much of the weak reported realization. Before that investment and after removing ₹5.0518 crore customer-deposit support, cash is ₹10.8105 crore. This does not undo lease capital requirements. FY26 customer deposits and payables also support cash by ₹3.8891 crore and ₹2.9707 crore. Receivables over one year fell to ₹0.2960 crore from ₹0.5716 crore, with no provision. FY26 cash capex is ₹27.0429 crore; CWIP transfers are not counted twice. Cash ₹7.5686 crore is not all free: deduct ₹5 crore pledged FD and ₹1.057 crore IPO issue-cost earmark to obtain a conservative ₹1.5116 crore. An overlap sensitivity avoids pretending the restriction split is independently bank-confirmed. Gross debt is ₹18.0168 crore. Operating property is already in operating earnings value; neither it, TDS nor landlord deposits is added as a separate liquidation asset.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Use an after-rent enterprise-value model, not an Ind AS pre-rent EBITDA multiple. The stale ₹173 reference and March balance sheet imply ₹86.2588 crore EV after netting only conservatively free cash: 32.67× reported PAT, 10.20× operating EBITDA and 13.88× conservative normalized EBITDA. These are conditional historical bridges, not current executable multiples. The model dates every interval from March 2026 through the October 2031 terminal, including an explicit pre-entry period and January 2027 facility event. It calibrates management seats/occupancy to FY26 revenue without pretending the implied desk yield is an observed market price. New seats require upfront fit-out and landlord deposits, three months before commissioning and a further six-month occupancy ramp. Cash is checked before positive interval receipts as well as at period end; refundable client deposits, operating working capital, old statutory/tax obligations, maintenance, term principal and facility renewals are included once. Remaining non-Bangalore CWIP provides only a prior-spend credit, not free cash. Base, bull and bear expansion paths exhaust stated facilities and are unfinanceable without incremental funding under these assumptions; their non-rescue IRRs and entry prices are null, including any pre-entry breach. A separately labeled slow staged path is conditionally funded under renewal assumptions but yields an unattractive return at the reference price. Hypothetical rescue cases issue whole shares before interval uses, deduct 3% fees and distinguish ownership dilution from share-count expansion; no such proceeds are claimed received. All ordinary returns remain withheld while current obligations are unresolved. A funded reverse solution varies post-entry blended yield only, checks both endpoints and residual, and requires roughly 8% annual yield growth alongside the staged capacity plan and an 8× terminal multiple to meet a 15% hurdle. It is a conditional feasibility requirement, not a price target. Two-way capacity-growth/multiple, occupancy/fit-out and staged-yield/multiple grids plus reserve, maintenance, collections, renewal, tax, depreciation and variable-rent stresses show the fragility.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear argument is that apparent growth is a capital-intensive rental spread rather than durable high-return compounding. A customer exit lowers occupied seats and forces deposit refunds before fixed landlord rent, payroll and financing commitments adjust. A fit-out delay produces rent without fees; an adverse landlord dispute can strand capital as Bangalore already demonstrates. Front-loaded receivable or GST/advance recovery stress, deposit demands and January DOD non-renewal can then require outside equity at an unfavorable price. The linked bear case combines 70% occupancy, no yield growth, 6% rent escalation, slower collection, higher maintenance and 11% borrowing cost, rather than applying an arbitrary stock-price haircut. Its cash-floor breach precedes the assumed entry date, so there is no valid non-rescue investment IRR. A prefunded rescue sensitivity still leaves terminal equity recovery at zero under this severe case; the dilution and funding numbers are diagnostic, not a forecast or a claim of actual distress. Counterevidence is the clean reported default record, disclosed unused facilities, improved old receivables, potentially matched long-duration enterprise contracts and a revenue-sharing lease component. The thesis-break variable is sustained cash after occupancy-related rent, refundable deposits and reinvestment, not reported revenue alone. D3 reflects material impairment/adverse recapitalization risk across credible stresses, without converting an uncertain price or modeled reserve breach into a proven insolvency event.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A five- or tenfold share-price outcome requires much more than another period of high revenue growth. The embedded feasibility table translates the required equity value into after-rent EBITDA at 8×, then revenue at an explicitly assumed 20% margin and occupied seats at the terminal blended yield. It holds current shares for arithmetic only and subtracts terminal debt while preserving the required operating reserve; landlord deposits, pledged FD and operating property receive no extra value. Its revenue growth denominator is explicitly labeled and the full financing model is the controlling constraint. The enterprise would have to scale far beyond current revenue, secure sites and clients, pay fit-out/deposits and maintain occupancy without excessive dilution. The fastest modeled rollout already requires additional financing even in the bull operating case. ESOP full-pool dilution and any future rescue further raise the earnings needed per original share. Therefore neither 5× nor 10× is an evidence-supported funded investment case today; these are hurdle calculations, not promotional upside targets.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: 1. Track audited revenue and managed/cowork split against FY26 ₹35.4785 crore and 62.48% managed share; growth accompanied by further cowork erosion requires an explanation. 2. Reconcile active seats and mature/new-centre occupancy against 4,373 seats/85%; sustained mature occupancy below 75% is an analyst warning threshold, not a disclosed covenant. 3. Obtain operating start and recoverability evidence for Bangalore ₹5.5033 crore before assigning earnings or release value. 4. Compare new-location deposits, fit-out cost per seat and commissioning dates with the ₹1.10 lakh prospectus baseline; more than six extra months delay or material cost overruns require model revision. 5. Verify DOD extension before 21 January 2027 and cash/draw eligibility against the ₹13.1329 crore March headroom, including SOD collateral. 6. Reconcile the monetary April–July lease pipeline and essential twelve-month uses before any new-purchase recommendation. 7. Track CFO both as reported and after landlord/customer deposit movements; rising aged receivables or refundable-deposit dependence weakens CASH. 8. Separate expense capitalization, deferred-tax credit and other income from operating/per-share earnings every half-year; recurring policy deferral without cash returns weakens EARN/CAP. 9. Track related-party ₹10.5 crore deposits/advances, ESOP grants/exercise price and any guarantees. 10. Authenticate BSE 20/60-session turnover, zero-trade classifications, spread/depth and restrictions before sizing a 600-share-lot purchase. The next scheduled financial review is the FY27 first-half filing when available, not an invented publication date.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Research hold for a new investment. BQS4.9 is not high-quality-compounder territory and GQS6.0 does not offset weak normalized earnings, low recent committed-capital returns or missing current funding evidence. Quality and growth-quality points are numerically comparable at Medium confidence, with conditional gates and ±score uncertainty visible; the investment ranking remains excluded because IAS is NS and G3/G4 are unresolved. Do not call the company Avoid–governance without severe adverse evidence, and do not force a numerical funding cap when failure is not established. No ordinary buy price, target return or deployable position is issued. The conditional slow-growth or rescue prices in the model are scenario outputs only and cannot release the hold. Reconsider only after authenticating the operating/lease/capex/renewal bridge and executable quote/liquidity, then rerun the full cash model and R/P/L scores. A lower stock price alone cannot solve unquantified lease obligations or make a proposed trade executable. Existing holders should separately consider their own liquidity and loss capacity; this report is not personalized financial advice or a transaction instruction.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary coverage includes the complete FY25/FY26 annual financial statements with main audits, CARO and IFC; the final prospectus and restated cash flows; the May audited results, presentation and earnings call; September AGM voting; and April–July lease disclosures. Working original/mirror links, dates, hashes, locators and source arbitration are preserved below. Audit opinions are not substituted for reading annexures, and an aggregation-feed label is not evidence of a corporate action. Safe financial extracts preserve calculations but do not independently authenticate a replacement for the originals. Core open questions are the full monetary minimum-rental/lock-in maturity schedule, centre-specific capex/deposit commitments and return timing, operational-cohort and contracted-client profitability, current draw conditions and January renewals, exact deferred-cost depreciation, tax/TDS settlement timing, and complete dated BSE trading evidence. Models assume calibrated blended prices, conservative upfront cash availability, explicit maintenance and fixed-cost recurrence beyond IPO budgets, no dividends, no operating-asset double count and no optional ESOP proceeds. The baseline conservatively treats rent as fixed; a separate sensitivity makes the disclosed Krishna rent revenue-linked. All ND values remain missing rather than zero. The readable report summarizes full historical, annual scenario and sensitivity rows; the companion canonical record embeds every dated model row and calculation input.

facts: Related-party deposits and fit-out advances total ₹10.5 crore, or 25.36% of equity.
The prior ₹19.0115 crore related guarantee was removed in July 2025; the secretarial report states that the compounding matter was resolved.
evidence.counterevidence: The unmodified audit reports no fraud. Commercial RPTs and an approved ESOP are not themselves abuse.

facts: A portfolio of 4,373 seats is much smaller than national operators.
Management describes commodity competition; realized proprietary AI economics are not demonstrated.
evidence.counterevidence: Longer managed contracts and existing landlord relationships provide some switching friction.

facts: Revenue grew from ₹10.8807 crore in FY23 to ₹35.4785 crore in FY26.
H2FY26 revenue was ₹18.5636 crore versus ₹14.3748 crore; no business combinations were identified.
evidence.counterevidence: FY26 full-year growth of 23.60% is below FY25, and managed expansion masks coworking contraction.

facts: Managed revenue of ₹22.1666 crore represents 62.48% of FY26 sales.
April–July 2026 site announcements include 75,000 square feet at Okaya and 12,000 at Best Sky Tower.
evidence.counterevidence: Signed space is not occupied revenue. Flexible coworking exits and an incomplete client backlog schedule limit confidence.

facts: FY23–FY26 incremental NOPAT of ₹1.69425 crore divided by incremental IC of ₹52.8078 crore is 3.2083%.
Earlier FY22–FY24 incremental returns were 20.196%; the FY26 conservative normalized increment is near zero.
evidence.counterevidence: Large immature CWIP and deposits depress current returns; better utilization could improve economics.

facts: Comparable FY24–FY26 CFO/PAT is 7.8857%, with ₹15.4369 crore invested in landlord deposits.
Before landlord investment and net of customer-deposit support, cash is ₹10.8105 crore. Receivables over one year fall from ₹0.5716 crore to ₹0.2960 crore.
evidence.counterevidence: Customer deposits rose ₹3.8891 crore and payables ₹2.9707 crore in FY26, supporting CFO. Deposits remain real capital needs.

facts: Reported cash of ₹7.5686 crore becomes conservatively free cash of ₹1.5116 crore after pledged FD and IPO earmark.
Debt is ₹18.0168 crore; DOD of ₹6.9744 crore requires renewal beyond 21 January 2027.
evidence.counterevidence: Disclosed face-value headroom is ₹13.1329 crore, equity ₹41.4052 crore, and the audit reports no default.

facts: Management reports 25 centres, 4,373 seats and approximately 85% occupancy.
Bangalore fit-out of ₹5.5033 crore remains unavailable because of landlord issues.
evidence.counterevidence: The managed segment expanded strongly; the future one-million-square-foot target is not treated as missed before its due date.

facts: FY26 PAT grew 3.55%, but reported EPS declined to ₹5.30 from ₹7.53.
KMP/travel capitalization of ₹1.0933 crore and brand deferral of ₹1.15 crore materially raise reported earnings; H2 PAT declined.
evidence.counterevidence: The audit is unmodified and operating EBITDA excluding other income grew. Conservative normalized EBIT retains all recorded depreciation.

facts: The base path breaches the cash floor, suppressing its conditional IRR.
Explicit prefunded rescue cases are separately diluted and never assumed received.
evidence.counterevidence: A conditionally funded staged path and verified reverse solver provide useful feasibility diagnostics.

facts: A 70% occupancy, no-yield-growth and higher-cost case creates a pre-entry funding breach.
Even the prefunded bear rescue has zero terminal equity under the chosen assumptions.
evidence.counterevidence: No actual default is established; available headroom, deposit recovery and matched enterprise contracts may mitigate stress.

facts: ₹173 is the 14 October secondary last trade, not the 19 October executable close.
The funded staged 8× reverse case requires roughly 8% post-entry yield growth to meet a 15% hurdle.
evidence.counterevidence: Historical bridge multiples and reverse requirements are transparent but conditional.

facts: The official lot is 600 shares; the last secondary observed trade was 600 shares and ₹103,800.
Absence from 60 NSE files reflects a venue mismatch, not zero-volume history.
evidence.counterevidence: The dated normal-market master shows eligibility; there is no evidenced suspension.

summary: Nukleus Office Solutions leases, fits out and operates flexible workspaces and enterprise managed offices. Organic revenue expanded rapidly, with managed offices now the main growth engine, but earnings per share and returns on the enlarged capital base do not yet establish a compounder. The decisive strength is demonstrated customer demand and an operating portfolio, not a unique technology moat. The decisive risks are upfront fit-out and landlord deposits, rent commitments before occupancy, related-party capital exposure and material new expense capitalization. At the last independently corroborated secondary trade of ₹173 on 14 October 2026, the shares are not demonstrably cheap after normalization. Classification: research hold for a new investment, with growth/execution rather than income or asset-liquidation economics. A complete monetary lease pipeline, funded rollout and renewal bridge, consistent cohort cash returns and executable market evidence could change this conclusion. This is not a finding of default, fraud or debt restructuring.
